newsitem.title: UK: Pensions make the heart grow fonder - UK survey.
newsitem.headline: Pensions make the heart grow fonder - UK survey.

text.p: British men and women are more likely to look twice at a potential partner if they have a pension, according to research released on Monday from British insurance company Eagle Star.

The study, conducted to coincide with Valentine's Day on February 14, showed that more than two-fifths of men (43 percent) admit they were attracted to women with long-term financial security, such as pensions of their own.
Nearly half (48 percent) of the women questioned said men with long-term financial security have an attractive presence about them.

The survey suggests that British lovers have a sensible approach to money. Four-fifths of men and women (80 percent) said their ideal partner would have a pension so they could live comfortably in old age.
Over three-fifths (65 percent) admitted they are worried about maintaining living standards in old age.
The Eagle Star study showed that the romantic ideal of "live now, pay later" is becoming increasingly dated.
Nearly three-fifths of the single people questioned (58 percent) said they would only agree with this philosophy if they actually had a partner who could afford to pay later.
But a romantic minority of 12 percent still said wealth is definitely not the source of true love.

The research also showed differences between the sexes in their attitudes to love and money. Two-thirds of women (69 percent) say the prospect of financial security is an important part of romance while 51 percent of men said the promise of financial security is unimportant in an ideal partner.

Steve Roberts, director responsible for life and pensions at Eagle Star Direct, said romance was no longer enough. "True love may last forever, but it doesn't pay the bills and more people than ever recognise this and value financial security.
The was conducted for Eagle Star Direct by NOP Solutions in a telephone survey of 970 adults aged 16 and over during the weekend of January 31-February 2.
